title: CORE-6969 · homepage case-study video renders doubled captions
body:
**Linear:** [CORE-6969](https://linear.app/bsq-group/issue/CORE-6969) · **PR** #117

Premise confirmed. The MP4 already carries **burned-in subtitles**; the clone marked the auto-generated
VTT track `default`, so the browser drew it on top of them — two caption lines at once.

The spelling gives it away: the burned-in subtitle reads **"Chilli"**, the auto-generated VTT reads
**"Chili"**, and in the clone both are on screen simultaneously.

Measured off the `<video>`'s live `textTracks` at t = 14.36s, same file, same 1170x658 box:

| | `<track default>` | `textTrack.mode` | active cues |
|---|---|---|---|
| live | absent | `disabled` | none |
| clone before | **present** | **`showing`** | `["Chalk and Chili is a content production"]` |
| clone after | absent | `disabled` | none |

Live and clone reference the **same** `.vtt` and `.mp4` URLs — the only difference was `default`.
The VTT was also checked for duplicated cues as an alternative cause: 34 cues, none duplicated.

## The change

`AutoplayVideo.tsx:62` — dropped the `default` attribute. The track is kept, exactly as live keeps it,
so captions stay selectable from the player's own menu; this only stops them being force-enabled on load.

`srcLang`/`label` deliberately retained: live has neither, but they only name the track in that menu,
have no visual effect, and are not what caused the defect. Removing them would be a small a11y
regression for no fidelity gain.

## Scope

`AutoplayVideo` has exactly one consumer passing captions — the `CaseStudyVideo` block
(`CaseStudyVideo/Component.tsx:39`). It is the only `<track>` on the site; live's
`/company-formation-packages/` and `/about-us/` carry none.
acceptanceCriteria: Only one caption line renders — the video's burned-in subtitle, as on live.
textTrack.mode is disabled on load, matching live.
Captions remain selectable from the player controls.
No other block regressed — CaseStudyVideo is the only consumer.
